scenes.line1: How does Go keep goroutines safe?
scenes.say: Ever wondered how Go keeps goroutines from stepping on each other? Which tool keeps your code safe and fast?

scenes.label: Mutex
scenes.sub: Locks code so only one goroutine can run it at a time.
scenes.say: Mutex locks a section so only one goroutine can run it at once. It's your basic safety net.
WaitGroup waits for goroutines to finish. Once runs code just one time, even with many goroutines. Atomic lets you update variables without locks.

scenes.code:
var mu sync.Mutex
mu.Lock()
// critical section
mu.Unlock()
scenes.say: Here’s the classic mutex move. Lock before the critical section, unlock after. Keeps things safe.

scenes.question: What causes a mutex deadlock?
scenes.right: Locking in different orders or not unlocking
scenes.say: A common interview trap: Deadlocks happen when goroutines lock in different orders or forget to unlock. Always lock and unlock in a consistent way.
